content.title: About
content.content: Crackers are thin, crunchy biscuits made from wheat flour, water, vegetable fats and a modest amount of salt. The reduced‑sodium version contains roughly half the salt of regular saltine crackers, making it a better choice for those monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crackers originated in the United States in the early 19th century as a convenient way to preserve bread.
Reduced sodium is achieved by replacing part of the salt with flavor enhancers and spices.
Crackers are often used as a base for canapés and snack bites.
In some countries they are served with soup instead of bread.
Their light texture makes them easy to transport and store.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: The reduced salt level helps maintain normal blood pressure for individuals limiting sodium consumption.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat flour provides a slow‑release source of energy, contributing to prolonged satiety.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions are enriched with fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Crackers pair well with low‑fat cheeses, hummus, or vegetable dips, allowing for a balanced snack.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based crackers contain gluten and may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Some formulations include vegetable oils, so individuals watching fat intake should read the label.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: While most savory crackers are not sweet, a small amount of sugar is sometimes added for flavor balance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crackers can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, spread with low‑fat cream cheese, hummus, avocado, or used as a base for bite‑size canapés with vegetables and seafood.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store crackers in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep the bag tightly closed to retain crispness and prevent moisture absorption.
